newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sinar Mas to channel exports through Amcol.
newsitem.headline: Sinar Mas to channel exports through Amcol.

text.p: Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group plans to use Singapore-based Amcol Holdings as a distributor of the group's various export products, the Bisnis Indonesia daily reported on Tuesday.
The paper quoted group president director Eka Tjipta Widjaja as saying they would use Amcol as an operational base to support their exports.
Widjaja did not say which of the company's exports, which include paper, pulp and palm oil, were expected to be sent through the company.
"By having a listed company overseas, we won't have to spend huge funds to set up an institution which will be able to support our exports," Widjaja told the daily.
He also said it would be easier to raise cheaper funds offshore through an overseas listed company.
Sinar Mas agreed in August to buy and transform the troubled Amcol, a trading and property group, and to inject US$2.0 billion in assets.
"The acquisition is still under negotiation as the Stock Exchange of Singapore has not given a final decision on the Amcol conditions. So, it still belongs to other people," Widjaja said.
Amcol was placed under interim judicial management in July after a Price Waterhouse report said the company had serious cashflow problems and difficulty meeting financial obligations.
